tools.name: nookal_list_locations
tools.description: List the clinic's locations (id, name, address, time zone, active). Location ids are needed by most other tools. Only the locations your API client was granted are returned. Nookal GraphQL: locations.

tools.name: nookal_list_staff
tools.description: List staff members and practitioners (id, name, title, speciality, email, location ids, whether they are a provider / bookable online / active). Use the staff ids as provider_ids in list_appointments and staff_ids in get_availability. Nookal GraphQL: staff.

tools.name: nookal_list_services
tools.description: List the appointment types / services offered (id, name, category, duration in minutes, price, location, online-booking settings). Use a service id in get_availability. Nookal GraphQL: services.

tools.name: nookal_list_classes
tools.description: List the class types offered (id, name, category, duration, price, location, online-booking settings) — the class definitions, not individual sessions. Nookal GraphQL: classes.

tools.name: nookal_get_availability
tools.description: Get the free appointment slots per date between two dates (max 60 days, Nookal's limit), optionally for given locations, practitioners and a service. Each slot has its date, start time (24h, clinic local time), provider id and location id. Read-only: it does not book anything. Nookal GraphQL: availa

tools.name: nookal_list_appointments
tools.description: List appointments (date, start/end time, status, type, client, practitioner, case, location, arrived / did-not-arrive flags, notes), filtered by date range, location, client, practitioner, type and status. Dates are clinic local. Nookal GraphQL: appointments.

tools.name: nookal_search_clients
tools.description: Find clients (patients) by name, date of birth, mobile, email or id. Returns id, name, date of birth, location, active/deceased flags and contact details. With partial_match, names match on their first letters (e.g. 'Sm' finds Smith). Nookal GraphQL: clients.

tools.name: nookal_get_client
tools.description: Get one client (patient) by id: name, date of birth, contact details, addresses, alerts, allergies, notes, occupation, referring doctor and their treatment cases; optionally a summary of their invoices (totals and balances). Health-fund, pension and online-booking codes are not returned. Nookal Grap

tools.name: nookal_list_cases
tools.description: List treatment cases (id, client, title, start and referral dates, referrer, primary practitioner, notes), filtered by client, case or practitioner. Nookal GraphQL: cases.

tools.name: nookal_list_invoices
tools.description: List invoices with their line items and payments (number, client, case, location, practitioner, date, subtotal, tax, total, paid, balance), filtered by location, invoice id or creation date. For one client's invoices use get_client with include_invoices. Nookal GraphQL: invoices.

tools.name: nookal_list_payments
tools.description: List payments received against invoices (method, amount, date, reference, invoice, client, location), filtered by invoice or payment date. Nookal GraphQL: payments.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: nookal_list_staff, nookal_search_clients · Private data: nookal_search_clients, nookal_get_client · Public sink: nookal_list_staff, nookal_search_clients.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: nookal_list_staff, nookal_search_clients · Private data: nookal_search_clients, nookal_get_client · Public sink: nookal_list_staff, nookal_search_clients

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
